messages:
Talia (PM): Hey team — trying to reconcile field asks for private deploy packaging with our upgrade constraints. quick poll: do we prioritize a slim operator (fast onboarding) or a richer operator+relay that supports customer-managed networking (preserve egress IPs, BGP handoff)?
Raj (Eng-Infra): For runtime simplicity I like slim operator, but relay buys us a lot for customers behind strict netops. preserves egress IP is a common ask.
Marta (Field): Customers keep asking for egress preservation and BGP handoff. Many large customers will not accept NAT hairpin. They'd rather us provide an operator+relay pattern they can opt into.
Eli (Security): Relay surface increases attack surface and audit needs. We need clear KMS/HSM integration, mTLS for control plane, and audit logs before shipping relay. If slim operator can't meet egress, we risk blocking big deals.
Sam (CS): Agreed with Marta. Small customers prefer slim. Enterprise deals ask for relay and deterministic IPs. We should offer both but make one GA first.
Talia (PM): Proposal: GA ship = slim operator + an "upgrade path" to opt-in operator+relay. Launch criteria for GA: preflight checks, zero-data-loss operator upgrades, and documented rollback window. Relay goes GA in Q2 after security review. Thoughts?
Raj (Eng-Infra): Sounds sensible. Need to define upgrade path clearly: operator patch upgrade (in-place, minor) vs blue-green for relay. For relay opt-in we should offer a one-command migration: `rdeploy attach-relay --tenant <id>`
Marta (Field): One-command is great, but we must ensure runbook for NetOps: e.g., BGP session test, IP preserve validation. Customers will want a dry-run mode.
Eli (Security): Dry-run + telemetry opt-in required. Also add an automated validation that verifies TLS cert rotation before cutover.
Talia (PM): I'll write acceptance criteria. Draft checklist:```
- preflight: kube version, storage class, nodes available
- network dry-run passes (BGP/NAT checks)
- KMS/HSM integration smoke pass
- TLS cert rotator verified
- rollback-tested in staging
```
Raj (Eng-Infra): Add: `operator.v1.upgrade_safe=true` feature flag for in-place upgrades. And a migration tool that records step timestamps to help rollback diagnostics.
Sam (CS): Can we add a customer-visible SLA doc for the relay path (expected downtime during upgrade, rollback window)? Sales will need numbers.
Marta (Field): Yes — propose 30m expected upgrade window for in-place operator, 90m for relay-assisted migration (includes BGP convergence). We should validate those in our canary customers.
Talia (PM): Action items: 1) Raj: design migration CLI + feature flag (owner). 2) Eli: list security gating items for relay (owner). 3) Marta: pick two customers for canary relay dry-runs (owner). 4) Sam: prepare SLA blurb for sales (owner). I'll draft the acceptance criteria doc and link it here when ready.
Raj (Eng-Infra): Working on a quick prototype. Early note: relay needs ephemeral control-plane tunnels for initial handshake, customers prefer a config that avoids opening inbound ports. We'll prototype a reverse-tunnel pattern.
Eli (Security): Reverse-tunnel pattern acceptable if we authenticate with short-lived certs and HSM-backed keys. I'll specify constraints.
deploy-bot: Deploy queued: priv-operator v1.0.0-alpha -> staging (started) :rocket:
Sam (CS): thanks — once staging passes, can we run a scripted dry-run with sample BGP session? Marta can coordinate.
Marta (Field): I'll schedule with customer A next week for dry-run. We should capture timing and failure modes.
Talia (PM): Great. Last note: prioritize docs and runbooks — customers will judge this heavily. I'll add doc owners to the checklist. Closing thread for now, will post acceptance criteria link when done. :white_check_mark:
